+# Restructure `ai-resources` to mirror the AI-agents talk
+
+## Context
+
+Lucas is giving the talk **"AI Agents for Economic Research & Teaching"** (`presentations/AI_Exchange_Agents/main.tex`) this week. The public GitHub repo `ai-resources` should be the place a visitor lands *right after* the talk and recognizes its structure — every concept the talk walks through should map to a clearly-labeled spot in the repo.
+
+Today the repo has **drifted** from what the talk actually demos:
+- **No hooks at all**, although hooks are concept #7 in the talk and Lucas has 6 clean, shareable ones live.
+- The **`log/current.md` memory pattern** and **MCP/Zotero setup** are never documented as visitor-facing resources.
+- The **skills set is stale**: repo ships `critic`, `scholar`, `devils-advocate` (all retired — none exist in the live config) and `empirical-paper-summarizer` (renamed to `summarize-paper`); the talk-referenced `blindspot`, `germancheck`, `council` are absent.
+
+**Outcome:** a repo whose top-level README is a guided tour of the talk, with the agentic section reorganized into one folder per talk concept (in talk order), the live skills and hooks shipped and sanitized, and a `presentations/` folder holding the talk(s).
+
+Decisions already made with Lucas:
+- **Structure:** mirror the talk — one labeled folder per concept, walkable in order.
+- **Skills (10 to ship):** `summarize-paper`, `referee2`, `blindspot`, `germancheck`, `econ-write`, `revise`, `deck`, `tikz`, `council`, `premortem`.
+- **Slides:** a `presentations/` folder (plural — holds this talk plus older ones).
+- `devils-advocate` is **not** a live skill → archive it with `critic` and `scholar`.
+
+---
+

+
+### 1. `presentations/` folder
+- Create `presentations/ai-agents-research-teaching/`; copy `main.pdf`, `main.tex`, `cookie_monster.jpg` from `/Users/lucasbuetje/code_macbook/presentations/AI_Exchange_Agents/` (compiled PDF is current, 28 Jun). Do **not** copy build artifacts, the `demo/` folder, or `session-07.*`.

Make the narrative coherent with `1-context`: e.g. `guard-rm.sh` enforces the "mv to archive" rule shipped in `global-CLAUDE.md`.
+
+### 5. `1-context/` — CLAUDE.md examples
+- `global-CLAUDE.md`: a **curated, sanitized** subset of Lucas's live global rules — only the genuinely general ones the talk surfaces: File Preservation, Scope Boundary, Raw Data (run don't read), Progress Log, Surgical Editing, Minimal Code, Objective Partner, Verification Is Code, German Writing Conventions, Em-Dash Restraint. Drop everything personal (Obsidian, Zotero specifics, PhD task board, jobsearch, course tooling). This expands the repo's current 7-rule template.
+- `project-CLAUDE.md`: a short, realistic example of a per-project file (data location, build command, codebook path) — matching the talk's "Local" column.
+

+Rewrite the root `README.md` to open with **"Just saw the talk? Start here"** and follow the talk's arc, each section linking into the matching folder:
+1. **What is an AI agent?** — chatbot vs agent, "it can do anything your computer can," risks, built-in safeguards (condensed from talk Section 1; reuse existing risk prose).

+3. **The reveal** — every session is saved as `~/.claude/projects/<dir>/<id>.jsonl`; reproducible and auditable (talk Section 3).
+4. **AI Chat (bonus)** — keep the existing CRISPE section, framed as the "chatbot" side of the talk's slide 2.
+5. **Other tools** + link to `presentations/`.
+Keep the disclaimer, the Claude Code vs OpenCode+GWDG table, and Scott Cunningham attribution.

+- `.gitignore`: add `.DS_Store`, `.Rhistory`; `git rm --cached` the tracked `.DS_Store` files (working copies untouched — not a Rule #1 deletion).

+# AI Resources
+
+How I use AI **agents** for academic research and teaching — the setups, conventions, and skills I actually rely on day-to-day. Reach out: lucas.buetje.economist@outlook.com
+
+**Disclaimer:** Everything here is provided as-is. Use at your own risk. I'm not responsible for any data loss or other issues that arise from using it.
+
+## How to use this repo
+
+- **This is a menu, not a template.** Don't clone it and expect it to "work" — it's meant to inspire and to be picked from. Take what fits how you work, adapt it, ignore the rest.
+- **Agentic AI is the focus.** An agent acts on your computer — reads and writes files, runs commands, completes multi-step tasks. That's where the leverage is, so that's what this repo is about.
+- Plain AI chat and other tools still have their place, but they're a footnote here → [`non-agentic/`](non-agentic/).
+- **New to this?** Install a tool first: [`getting-started/`](getting-started/).
+
+## What an AI agent is
+
+- It runs *inside a project folder*: it reads, writes, and runs commands there, and (by default) can't reach above it. That folder is its whole world.
+- Think of it as a fast, capable research assistant that starts every session with **no context and no memory** — the pieces below are how you give it both, keep it safe, and check its work.
+- Because it can run any terminal command, it can in principle do *anything* your computer can. *(Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Windsurf.)*
+
+## What it can (and can't) safely do
+
+- **Risks worth knowing:**
+  - File access is real — files can be overwritten or deleted.
+  - Plugins (MCPs) from untrusted sources can run malicious code on your machine.
+  - Anything sensitive in the working folder (keys, credentials, personal data) is readable.
+  - Errors compound — a wrong assumption gets confidently built upon.
+- **Built-in safeguards:** permission prompts before actions, plan/read-only mode, confinement to the working folder, visible diffs before changes apply.
+- **Stay alert anyway:** safeguards can fail, the tools keep changing, and permission pop-ups get clicked away. Use plan mode, keep backups / version control, and install only what you trust.
+
+## How I use an agent well
+
+The pieces below, in the order they matter. Each links to its folder or to its section here.
+
+### 1. Context — [`claude-md/`](claude-md/)
+- A `CLAUDE.md` the agent reads at the start of every session, so you stop re-explaining yourself.
+- **Global** (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`): how *you* work — applies everywhere. See [`global-CLAUDE.md`](claude-md/global-CLAUDE.md).
+- **Project** (`<project>/CLAUDE.md`): what *this* project is — data locations, build commands, conventions. See [`project-CLAUDE.md`](claude-md/project-CLAUDE.md). Tip: run `/init` to have the agent draft it.
+
+### 2. Memory — [`memory-log/`](memory-log/)
+- Agents forget everything between sessions. One file, `log/current.md`, carries working memory forward.
+- The agent appends what changed and what's open; the next session reads it back in (automatically, with a SessionStart hook).
+
+### 3. Plan mode
+- The agent investigates and writes a **plan**, but changes nothing until you approve. The single most useful safety habit.
+- Without it: it edits immediately, and you find a wrong assumption *after* 12 files changed. With it: you fix the misunderstanding first.
+
+### 4. Skills — [`skills/`](skills/)
+- Reusable, named recipes invoked with one command (`/summarize-paper`, `/referee2`, …). Write the instructions once, reuse forever.
+- The 11 shipped here (mostly adapted from or inspired by Scott Cunningham — [his blog](https://causalinf.substack.com/s/claude-code)) are listed in [`skills/README.md`](skills/README.md).
+
+### 5. Subagents
+- The agent can spawn many subagents that work in parallel, each on a slice, then report back. Saves time, not tokens (N subagents ≈ N× the quota).
+- In practice: `/summarize-paper` fans out across a reading list; `/referee2` runs five specialist auditors at once; `/council` polls several models that critique each other.
+
+### 6. MCP
+- MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard plug for external tools. Each server is installed once, then the agent can call it.
+- Example: a **Zotero MCP** lets the agent answer "what papers do I have on X?" and pull a PDF (with your highlights) straight from your library.
+- **Caution:** an MCP runs code on your machine — install only servers you trust.
+
+### 7. Hooks — [`hooks/`](hooks/)
+- Small scripts the tool runs automatically at set moments (before a command, at session start, on stop). Your conventions, enforced by code instead of trust.
+- The ones shipped here back up rules from `global-CLAUDE.md` — e.g. `guard-rm.sh` blocks `rm` and points at `archive/`.
+
+### 8. Verification — [`verification/`](verification/)
+- Producing code/analyses is now cheap; *checking* them is the bottleneck. The agent is confident even when wrong.
+- Have it write re-runnable scripts that test against a known truth — see the runnable [`example-recovery-check.R`](verification/example-recovery-check.R).
+
+## Nothing is lost
+
+- Every session is saved as structured text at `~/.claude/projects/<working-dir>/<session-id>.jsonl`: the original prompt, every tool call, subagent, script, error, and retry.
+- The quiet fear is that AI work is a black box. It isn't — the full record sits on your machine, reproducible and auditable, ready to hand to a co-author or another agent.
+

+- **Not everything is an agent.** Prompts for plain AI chat (CRISPE-structured) and other tools I use (NotebookLM, Perplexity, literature search) live in [`non-agentic/`](non-agentic/).

+# Non-agentic AI
+
+The rest of my AI toolkit — plain chat tools and assistants that *don't* act on your computer. Useful, but secondary to the [agents](../README.md) this repo is mostly about.
+
+## AI Chat vs Agentic AI
+
+- **AI Chat** — you type, it replies with text. No access to your files or computer; it may produce files you download, but it can't act. *(Gemini, Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Perplexity.)*
+- **Agentic AI** — reads/writes files, runs commands, completes multi-step tasks on its own. That's the [main repo](../README.md).
+
+## Custom prompts for AI Chat
+
+- Prompts for any chat tool (Gemini, Claude.ai, ChatGPT), structured with the **CRISPE** framework.
+- **Store them somewhere reusable** (Gemini Gems, Claude Projects, …) — don't paste them into every new chat.
+
+### The CRISPE framework
+
+Credit: Alexis Castellanos (University of Michigan, [PDHP Workshop](https://psc.isr.umich.edu/events/ai-2/)).
+
+| Letter | Meaning | Example |
+|---|---|---|
+| **C** — Capacity | Define the persona | "Expert Applied Microeconomics Research Assistant" |
+| **R** — Role | Specific task | "Extract and audit causal identification strategies" |
+| **I** — Insight | Constraints/protocols | "NEVER use conversational filler" |
+| **S** — Style | Tone and formatting | "Telegraphic, strict LaTeX for math" |
+| **P** — Process | Step-by-step execution | Scan → Classify → Audit → Sanitize → Output |
+| **E** — Example | A perfect input/output pair | Shows the model exactly what you want |
+
+### The prompts
+
+| Custom AI | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| [Empirical Paper Summarizer](empirical_paper_summarizer.md) | Structured summary: data, identification strategy, main results |
+| [Review Paper Summarizer](review_paper_summarizer.md) | Summary of literature reviews and survey papers |
+| [Custom AI Creator](custom_ai_creator.md) | Meta-tool: drafts CRISPE prompts for new custom agents |
+| [Paper Podcast Prompter](notebooklm_paper_podcast_prompter.md) | NotebookLM instructions for podcast scripts from papers |
+| [Google Scholar Labs Prompter](google_scholar_labs_prompter.md) | Natural-language queries for Google Scholar Labs |
+
+- **Chat history:** Gemini doesn't save history without enabling data training. I use [SaveChat for Gemini](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/savechat-%E2%80%93-for-gemini-ai/blndbnmpkgfoopgmcejnhdnepfejgipe) to export and [this script](move_gemini_chats.sh) to file them.
+
+## Other tools
+
+- **[NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google.com):** upload documents for summaries, Q&A, or audio overviews — I turn a paper into a podcast for train rides.
+- **[Perplexity](https://perplexity.ai):** AI chat with web search and source-type toggles.

+# Plan mode
+
+The agent investigates and writes a **plan**, but changes *nothing* until you say go. The single most useful safety habit — and it needs no setup, it's built into the tool.
+
+## Why it matters
+
+| Without plan mode | With plan mode |
+|---|---|
+| It starts editing immediately | You read the plan first, fix the misunderstanding |
+| You discover a wrong assumption *after* 12 files changed | Only then does it touch your files |
+
+- The cost of a wrong assumption is paid *before* any file changes, not after.
+
+## When to use it
+
+- Anything non-trivial or multi-step — refactors, a new analysis, touching many files.
+- For small, well-defined tasks, skip it: just tell the agent what to do.
+
+## How
+
+- In Claude Code, enter plan mode before describing the task; the agent explores read-only, proposes a plan, and waits.
+- Read it, push back, refine — then approve. Treat the plan as the place to catch misunderstandings cheaply.

+# Subagents
+
+The agent can spawn **many subagents** that work in parallel — each on a slice of the task — then report back. One assistant becomes a team.
+
+## What it's good for
+
+- **Reading list:** [`/summarize-paper`](../skills/summarize-paper/) fans out across many papers at once — done in the time it takes to read one.
+- **Paper audit:** [`/referee2`](../skills/referee2/) runs five specialists simultaneously: code, replication, econometrics, structure, prose.
+- **LLM council:** [`/council`](../skills/council/) sends a question to several models; they critique each other and a chair synthesizes.
+
+> [!TIP]
+> **Example:** 30 papers on peer effects summarized and synthesized in a coffee break.
+
+## Saves time, not tokens
+
+- Running N subagents costs roughly **N× the quota** — they all think in parallel.
+- So the win is *wall-clock time*, not cost. Reach for them when the work splits cleanly into independent slices, not to save money.
+
+## You don't set this up
+
+- No manual wiring — just ask: "use one subagent per paper", "fan this out", "run these checks in parallel".

+# MCP — connecting the agent to other tools
+
+**MCP** (Model Context Protocol) is a standard plug for external tools. Each server is installed once, then the agent can call it — Zotero, a database, a browser, an issue tracker, whatever speaks MCP.
+
+## Example: the Zotero MCP
+
+With the Zotero MCP, I can:
+
+- 🔍 Ask "what papers do I have on X?" and have the agent search my library.
+- 📄 Let the agent pull a PDF straight from Zotero — including my own highlights and notes.
+
+That turns the agent from something that works *only* on files in the folder into something that reaches into the tools I already use.
+
+> [!CAUTION]
+> An MCP **runs code on your machine**, with the same reach as the agent. A malicious or careless server can do real damage. Install only servers you trust.
+
+## How to add one
+
+- Install the MCP server per its own docs.
+- Register it with your agent: `claude mcp add …` for Claude Code, or the MCP section of the OpenCode config.
+- Then just ask the agent to use it — it discovers the available tools on its own.
